groups.label: Structure and Scope of Dialogue
groups.summary: Commentary examines the overall significance of the Republic, framing it around an investigation of justice while analyzing whether its design forms five natural divisions or an imperfect two-part architectural contrast.
groups.rationale: All four entries evaluate the macro-structure, architectural design, and thematic scope of the Republic as an entire work.

groups.label: Moral Inquiries and Challenges
groups.summary: Commentary traces the evolution of moral stages and interlocutors from early conventional definitions to Glaucon and Adeimantus demanding that Socrates defend justice for its inherent nature rather than external consequences.
groups.rationale: These entries focus on the progressive dialectic, interlocutors' arguments, and specific challenges regarding the intrinsic versus extrinsic value of justice.

groups.label: State Design and Civic Classes
groups.summary: Commentary traces the construction of the civic order from the state-individual analogy to the formation of specialized guardians, social ordering via the Myth of the Metals, communitarian disciplines, and the four cardinal virtues.
groups.rationale: These items outline the sociopolitical architecture of the ideal city, class hierarchy, communal rules, and distribution of civic virtues.

groups.label: Guardian Cultural Education
groups.summary: Commentary details the rigorous curriculum for the guardian class, involving the purification of theology, strict limitations on dramatic imitation, reform of musical modes, and physical conditioning aimed at serving the soul.
groups.rationale: These entries all focus directly on the cultural, aesthetic, and physical education designed to properly form the character of the guardians.
